entities.summary: Stefano di Giovanni di Consolo, known as il Sassetta, was a Tuscan painter of the Renaissance and a significant figure of the Sienese School. He was born in Siena, Italy, and died in 1450. In 1435, il Sassetta was commissioned by the Sienese Republic to create a series of paintings for the Palazzo Pubblico. This work showcased his innovative style, which blended elements of Gothic decoration and realism. Il Sassetta's paintings were widely admired during his lifetime, and he was considered one of the leading artists of the Sienese School. In 1441, il Sassetta was elected as a member of the Arte della Lana, a guild of textile merchants in Siena. He was a prolific artist, producing over 100 paintings during his career. Il Sassetta's innovative style had a lasting impact on the development of Renaissance art. In 1450, il Sassetta died, leaving behind a legacy as one of the greatest painters of the Sienese School.
